construction: 14 parts in 1 step: a 2×4 plate on two 4870 2×2 plates with wheel pins, four 4624 rims with 3139 tyres pressed onto the pins, two 32530 1×2 tiles with two holes standing side by side on the plate, and a 2780 friction pin through their lower holes.
interfaces: Stud directions: 14 parts, 7 up, the standing tiles and wheels facing ±Z. The pin is the only connection to the parent; the wheels turn on their pins.
lesson: A compact main-gear bogie: two 2×2 wheel-pin plates under a 2×4 plate carry four small wheels; two 1×2 tiles with holes stand on the plate so that one friction pin through them is the whole mounting interface to the fuselage.
parent_context: `7893 - plane.ldr` places it twice with the identity matrix at Y 127, Z 64, X −150 and X +170: the two bogies are not symmetric about X=0 because the fuselage sections are offset one stud in the source. They hang under the wing root behind the engines.
reuse_notes: Use it under any minifigure-scale airliner or cargo plane: one pin hole per bogie in the fuselage or wing is enough, and the standing tiles set the leg height. Mirror the placement, not the part.
